t: The Return of the Bully: Once again Somaliland Militia terrorizes Historic Taleh
x: Somaliland Militia enter Taleh on June 12, 204. On June 12, 2014. Dozens of people have been reported injured, 4 in serious condition as Somaliland Militia equipped with 90 Technico vehicles attacked Khatumo's Historical city of Taleh. Somaliland Forces went into a firing spree in and around the areas of Khatumo administration's landmarks such as the Sayid Mohamed A. Hassan Airport, the famous Fig-Tree (Berdaha Khatumo) garden, and the main roads leading to the office of Khatumo President Mohamed J. Indho-sheel. Militia forces loyal to Somaliland administration started blocking entry points to Taleh around 8:00 a.m local time when the Khatumo civil society was planning to hold a peaceful Khatumo III conference to solidify their local administration established in the same City a year ago. Khatumo State of Somalia is a separate administration that was formed in last year's Grand Khatumo 2 Congress of the Sool, Sanaag, Cayn people in the city of Taleh. All 13 Traditional Graads and more than 65 Caqils along with 6000 civil society participants have unanimously declared their formal separation from Puntland and Somaliland. Somaliland's incursion comes amid recent visits to Taleh by thousands of local delegates from Sool Sanaag and Cayn regions, eager to participate in Khatumo's ratification of a new State Constitution and democratic elections for a new president. However, as the local people became aware of the dangers of renewed fighting in peaceful Taleh, the Traditional Elders along with Intellectuals from abroad and neighbouring khatumo cities have agreed to temporarily withdraw their forces from Taleh; allowing the invading Somaliland Militia to enter the city. Additionally, earlier in 2014, Somaliland was forced to withdraw its forces from the Taleh due to political pressures from the International Community including the Ethiopian government, EU, US, the British and Somali Government. So why did they come back now ! Somaliland claims that they entered into Taleh to disrupt the khatumo III Conference which is aligned with the Unionist principals of Somalia's Federal Government in Mogadishu; something that Somaliland opposes because of their Secessionist ideology. "It is also a matter of political survival for Somaliland's Silanyo" said Farah Abdulle, a long resident of Taleh City. "I lived my whole life in Taleh and Sool region, so many administrations lay claim to our city, but the local people have made their choice clear in January 2012 when they endorsed their Khatumo administration. Embroiled in its own so called parliamentary and political party squabbles and facing the loss of his own governing Party's confidence, Silanyo wants to divert the attention of his political base thus reverting to illegal attacks in distant khatumo lands" Continued Mr. Abdulle. "Khatumo administration condemns these barbaric atrocities and It is unfortunate that Somaliland has begun a new war in the region" stated Mukhtar Habashi , Khatumo administraton's chief of staff. "Khatumo People are committed to exercise their inalienable right to freedom of assembly and we will defend our people and our land" continued Mukhtar. A. t: Now officially open in Taleh City, Ladies and Gentlemen: Say hello to Khatumo III Conference and Elections 2014
x: (Khatumo.net) Taleh. Sunday June 8th 2014, The long awaited and much anticipated Khatumo III Conference has been declared open by President Mohamed Yusuf Indho-sheel and Graad Mohamud Osman Mashqare _ a member of Khatumo's Traditional Council. Along with members of the Khatumo Diaspora, Graad Abshir Salah, Dr. Ali Isse, have all arrived at Sayyid Mohamed Abdulle Airport to participate in the Conference. Hundreds of delegates from the Diaspora as well as from neighboring local townships such as Lasanod, Buhodle, Ceegaag, Widh-widh, Boame, Arroley, Dharkayn and finally Erigavo have gathered to participate in today's ceremonies in Taleh. "The people of Taleh have once again shown their support and true feelings toward their new Khatumo Administration", "We are confident that this will be another historic moment for the people of Sool Sanaag and Cayn as they transition to a more stable and solid Khatumo Administration" stated Graad Mashqare. Additionally, Khatumo Minister of International relations, Dr. Hussein Saleban Dhegawayne has called on the people of Khatumo to showcase their genuine support to this historic conference. "Don't just sit there and ask questions like who said what to whom, or what is the status of Khatumo III. There are so many bogus and biased information deliberately dessiminated by predatory administrations" cautioned Dr. Saleban. "I urge all the Khatumo Diaspora folks to travel to the region and see for their eyes the true economic and political status of their region, it requires true allegiance and blood support to your land If you are unable to travel to Taleh, please remember that you can support Khatumo in many other ways including financial support" added Dr. Saleban. Khatumo is the tie that binds and unites Sool Sanaag and Cayn. See our neighbors have constructed names for their regions and you wanna stay with ancient tribal names that has gotten you nowhere. We can have different viewpoints and perspectives and that is the hallmark of a young democracy like Khatumo. We can agree to disagree, we can use different avenues to achieve a common goal: khatumo is not perfect; it hasn't liberated lasanod yet, it has not fully crafted the state constitution yet, and its strategic planning has not been as transparent as you might have liked, However, like any other new democracy…It is the least worst system you have.. See …You need to work with your new found identity. Knowing that you are just against something is not going to get you anywhere. Too much chatter In the coffee shops and internet chat lines, Uttering mere condemnations against Khatumo is the work of the lazy. God will NOT judge you on how many ideas or things you have destroyed; God will judge you on how many things you have built up. Khatumo truly reignited the collective imagination of its people while safeguarding the security of its citizens. From water projects, and student scholarships to opening up the skyways of SSC region, Khatumo has already arrived, It is here, and will always be there for future generations of this land. After all you cannot put the toothpaste back into the tube. In search of solutions to your problems, some of you maybe still hung up on the old belief that you might be better off with aligning yourself with your neighbors to the right and left of khatumo State. See you have been confused, constantly looking at your right and left shoulders…Forgetting that your heart actually lied in between. Here…take a sip of self-esteem and ask your heart where it truly belongs? And as you discover the real you…Only then can you brush off the demons from your shoulders like this… And this… See… Khatumo needs you to trust and believe in it, because without you, it cannot actually grow or even exist. You need it to use it as your flashlight to guide you and illuminate the dark pathways that connect your underdeveloped towns and cities; cities that have been willfully abandoned and neglected by predatory administrations. With your help, Khatumo can flush out and shed light on the atrocities and political and economic injustices perpetrated against your people; With your support, Khatumo can help you to realize your dreams and aspirations for a better life. Students accross the Khatumo landscape can learn their Daraawiish history as told to them by their own historians. Young pregnant mothers who need medical help in Taleh and buhodle can be immediately transported and flown to overseas hospitals right from their own Airports. And now that Khatumo State has been legally recognized by the Somali Federal Government and thus United Nations entities, our Elders and seniors can finally proclaim and say that: We are not from Somaliland We are not from Puntland We are not from a disputed land, We are from the promise land of Khatumo State of Somalia. The Khatumo Candle, democratically lit up under that beautiful fig tree in Taleh city needs you. And you need it too; see, this new found identity does not belong to any one or two or three people; it belongs to the little girl in Sool-Jogto, it belongs to the seniors in Siixawle. It also belongs to the students in lasanod and business leaders in Buhodle. It belongs to all of us. There maybe a few among us who aren't so sure about Khatumo's accomplishments sometimes exhibiting self doubt or possibly even comfortable being in 2nd place in other administrations.These are the people who may try to divide you along the tribal lines of Faarah, or Mohamoud; Baho-Nugaaleed or Gabooye, Fiqishinni, or Kaskii-qabe. Just Hit the delete button and tell them that the days of contrarians and clan conspiratorialists are over. See…in the midst of Somalia's federal landscape, these communities are your branches of the Khatumo tree. In the current Somali politicking dominated by regional administrations and city states, the need to organize and exercise your constitutional right to self governance has never been greater. I understand that change is difficult, but Imagine the absence of Khatumo for a moment; Can you tell me who you are? See… you are left with your subclan tribal identity that will not serve you in the national and international political and economic negotiations. Khatumo is not against any particular group of people or administration; It does not go out and invade other people's territories, Khatumo simply advocates for the peaceful stay of its own God given land. It advocates for better Health, Education and Employment opportunities for its people. Khatumo advocates for the peaceful coexistence with all its regional neighbors. Is that too much to ask? See… for SSC folks, any identity other than Khatumo is a trip backwards to tribal land. Let's never move backwards to a disputed land; Together we can move forward to the blessed and promised land of Khatumo State. I ask the SSC and khatumo folks all over the world, Who do you think you were waiting for! The choice is clear, Ladies and gentlemen. "You" are the Ones you have been waiting for; God bless Khatumo State of Somalia. For more on this story, Stay with Khatumo.net A. Hindi: (admin@khatumo.net)

t: Western and China in New Cold War over Somali’s Oil Rich Regions in Northern Somalia’s tribal Secessionists (Somaliland) Aggressions to Khatumo State Regions Using UK Military Aid? …It’s the Oil, Stupid…
x: UK and USA oil majors have known about Somali's oil wealth since the early 1960's. In 1980's, Mohamed Siad Barre, Somalia' head of state, broke with the Soviets and invited Western oil companies to develop oil in the Somalia. That was perhaps a fatal mistake. Wars over oil have been the consequence even since. The crisis-wracked Somlia has been the site of Western corporate investment for a number of years. "Big Western companies including Conoco-Phillips, Chevron, and Shell held Somali exploration concessions before the country slid into civil war in 1990." But interest in Somalia's oil heated up dramatically over the past twenty years. Somalia may seem an unlikely prospect for investors seeking untapped oil and gas fields, but that could be about to change as the [oil] majors turn their gaze off the beaten track. Driven by record profits, a race with hungry Asian rivals and fears of growing energy nationalism in South America and Russia, interest in Somlia oil resources has never been higher. The recent aggressions from Northern tribal secessionists (Somaliland) in SSC regions are all the more clear given the abundance of resources in the area: massive amounts of oil in Khatumo State of Somalia. Western oil companies found big oil reserves in SSC regions of Somalia ( Hol Hol ). It spent $1.2 billion finding and testing them. That oil developments triggered what is called Somali's first civil war in 1990. Conoco was target of repeated attacks from Northern Tribal Secessionists (SNM) and suspended the project in 1989. Then China began to negotiate with Puntland leader (Abdillahi Yusuf Ahmed) in 2005 with no notable results. In recent months, British oil companies and UK politicians developed a close working relationship with the weak Somali Government at Mogadishu. Different UK delegates has embarked on a series of initiatives designed to secure long-term oil sources from one of the planet's most endowed regions the Horn of Africa region. Last week Puntland has signed oil and mineral development agreement with Chinese oil companies. No raw material has higher priority in Beijing at present than the securing of long term oil sources. These oil corporate practices have fuelled conflict and had a devastating impact on human rights. Leaked Oil companies data suggests that in 2013 alone, those companies spent $75 million on 'Other' unexplained security expenditures – a vast infusion of cash into the Somalia conflict. According to independent analysts, the distribution of cash and contracts by oil companies has contributed to "the killing and displacement of thousands of local people" in communal and tribal conflicts. Clandestine Oil-companies-gave-cash-and-contracts-to-militants-and-warlords-in- Somalia's northern tribal secessionists (Somaliland). This a crucial point and highlights how clandestine exploration licensing oil money gave northern tribal secessionists (Somaliland) the opportunity to peruse aggression options to SSC regions and therefore prolong the civil war the ant the misery for the people Somali people. t: Press Release : Somaliland Aggression
x: The intent of this press release is to express our objection to and condemnation of the on-going armed expansionist policies of the clan-based secessionist administration of Somaliland. For the last 7 years, the rulers of this unrecognized secessionist enclave has been occupying territories belonging to clans opposed to their secessionist agenda by force. These territories do not subscribe to the concept of seceding from the rest of the country. In 2007, the secessionist administration in Hargeisa occupied by force the city of Las-Anod, the capital of the unionist region of Sool, and has ever since been determined to occupy other districts in the surrounding areas. The administration has also embarked on a brutal invasion of the Ayn region and attempted to capture its capital city, Buhodle, killing and maiming in the process scores of innocent civilians defending their freedom and right to self-determination. During the current month, the Somaliland forces have moved to the historical town of Lasqorey and Badhan, the capital city of Makhir State, another unionist state in the east. During the last few days, the militias of this expansionist administration has been making overt and covert attempts to occupy fresh territories in the Sool and Sanag regions, including but not limited to Taleh town, the provisional capital of Khatumo state. All these attempts are designed to convince the international community of their complete control over the territories of the former British Protectorate of Somalia that gained its independence in 1960 and joined Italian occupied southern Somalia to form the Somali republic. They wrongly believe that the International community will recognize them as a country if they occupy all unionist territories by force. The actions of the clan dominated secessionist administration are more consistent with the medieval methods of imposing the will of few armed gangs on the public. To a large extent, the international community will be complicit in the actions of these modern day warlords in as far they turn a blind eye to their illegal actions, and inadvertently finance their war machinery through direct bilateral aid. Khatumo state, like other unionist states in Makhir and Awdal strongly believes in self-determination, freedom of expression and the right to remain part of the Federal Republic of Somalia, and will in no-doubt defend these God-given rights. In this regard and in view of the recent activities of Somaliland militia, we implore the international community to; 1. Take punitive measures against the Somaliland Administration for its unbridled aggression by imposing economic and financial sanctions against it until it withdraws its militia back to its well-defined territories and stop its aggression against the unionist regions that wish to remain within the fold of the Federal Republic of Somalia; 2. To provide development aid and humanitarian assistance to the peace loving unionist States in the area. Such regions have been neglected in the past and classified unfairly as disputed territories; 3. To allow unionist States like Khatumo state to play a prominent role in any future talks between the federal government and Somaliland since the latter does not necessarily represent the will of the all people in the region. 4. To send a strong message to the Somaliland administration in Hargeisa to pull back its forces that have been mobilized in the last few days to disrupt the Khatumo Conference that is scheduled to be held in Taleh in late April 2014. We hope that the international community and the federal government of Somalia shall assume their moral responsibility and stop the clan based aggression against our people. It is important for the stability of the region to contain the possible escalation of the situation and give peace a chance. Any aggression against Taleh, the provisional capital of Somalia can get out of hand and involve other regions in the area in the conflict. Mohamed Yusuf Jama President of Khatumo State of Somalia Taleh, Federal Republic of Somalia Note: Khatumo State is a recognized Federal State of Somalia that was established in January 2012. its leaders have recently travelled to Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia, and were welcomed warmly by the President , Prime Minister and Speaker of the Parliament of the Federal Government of Somalia. It strongly supports the unity and integrity of Somalia and desires to live in peace with its neighbouring Somali regions.

t: Lady Khatumo Wins the Final Battle of the Ball
x: Khatumo State of Somalia It is 5:00 pm on a Friday afternoon. Work at the office never finishes eh! But after a long commute, I arrive home and eat my usual spaghetti dinner. I made sure I had a good grip on my cup of fresh coffee before collapsing on my sofa. One glance at the television and it is Chelsea vs. Arsenal. "There is something oddly different about this ball game though," I wonder, as I gobble up larger and faster sips of my Khatumo Coffee. Suddenly, instead of a competition between two teams, I find myself watching three: the Traditional, Presidential and Executive Councils of Khatumo State, all converged in the midst of this large stadium, flexing their muscles as they get ready to play the Khatumo ball-game. Oblivious to the absence of a referee and even goal posts, each group hurries to kick the ball towards the direction each imagines to be the goal; up, down, right, left, loops, free kicks, it is open season. Nevertheless, the large crowd of Khatumites keeps cheering anytime they see beautiful ball movements. But as the game progresses, occasionally a ball would strike a player below the belt. "Stop the game," yells the fellow from the third row. "My uncle in team Presidential has been hit, you know, below the belt. I am sure that is a foul. A penalty is due." "What about my man in team Traditional, who during the first half was also wronged when he passed the ball East towards Garowe?" yells another fan from the second row. Meanwhile, burdened by a sense of responsibility to continue the game, team Executive keeps kicking the ball in any direction other than East or West. "So you are saying that all those games played over the past two years, the fans have been refereeing the Khatumo ball-games," said a voice from behind me. "There's gotta be a referee, you know. An authority to refer to whenever we need to settle our disputes or need guidance towards the right direction." "By the way," the voice continued, "are women allowed to play the Khatumo ball-game?" "Yes," I replied. "But they are limited to a few insignificant posts. Catching a stray ball here and there, you know." "So we are watching a political game between a few individuals whose common denominator is the fact that they are all men and old," said the voice, which by now seemed like that of a lady. "Well, I would not be that unkind, but that is kind of true," I finally conceded. Khatumo Grand Canyon (Lasanod Nov. 2013) "So who is that player with the number 5 shirt?" asked the Lady, pointing at team Presidential. "Oh, that is my uncle," I answered with pride. "He defends and leads this team so well, doesn't he. He is a brave man with two balls, geesi laba xiniinyood ah," I continued to brag. "So he must be a tough and strong fellow," said the Lady. "What do you mean by a strong fellow?" "You know. Strong leaders who do not rely on sub-clannish sentiment, and on outdated artificial titles, as a source of strength to disrupt their people's games and thus their wishes." "And how do you measure the strength of tough old fellows who can't get along?" "Certainly not by the size of their balls," said the Lady, and she giggled. "The older theirs are, the less productive they become." "You mean the less re-productive." "Perhaps that too," she laughed, genuinely this time, and I noticed she was letting me have that one. "The people's right to assemble freely in their hometown," she said instead. "Their right to debate, discuss and deliberate the direction of their local affairs. That should be a sacred duty. No rational person would disrupt such a gathering." And here the noise of the stadium went out of the afternoon altogether. "Travelling from Lasanod," she said, "were the same Khatumo ladies whose flowers were accepted last year. This year they were bullied and beaten and prevented from taking part in Khatumo III." She let that sit in the empty air where the cheering had been. "The people of Khatumo never changed their allegiance to their administration. So what changed?" I had nothing. Down on the field somebody was still moving the ball beautifully in no direction, and the crowd, when the sound came back, was still cheering it. "The paralysis hovering over Khatumo revolves around petty gripes between two parties," she went on. "He said this about you, and he said that about you. Meaningless personal grievances and gossip triangulated by a third party. So, what's the big deal if I said something as a joke and you found it offensive? Wouldn't you dismiss it as a non-issue?" "Perhaps," I said. "But only if it were up to me. See, anytime you take a little jab at an individual, you also have to deal with all the sub-clans of that person, who according to tradition would also appear to have been wronged, and feel entitled to damages by way of generalization." I wrongfully reasoned, and she let me hear myself do it. "Most wars in the world are about resources and land," she said. "Neither party here has caused the other physical damage. There is no land in dispute between them. Somaliland and Puntland have already wolfed up the land, save for Buhodle, where the flames of freedom are too hot to be extinguished. What is in dispute is a mere perception of foul mouth. And so the fate of nearly a million Khatumites is stalled because a few old men cannot settle a question of bad-mouthing. A few old men erroneously engaged in a waiting game of who blinks first, naively willing to go to their graveyard along with a Khatumo they never truly owned." Rainy season in Cayn region (Buhodle November, 2013) "Then who owns it?" "Ask who funds it. The fundamental question of who funds the Khatumo machinery should decide its eventual ownership, which puts the ball back in the corner of we the people. Before we start kicking it haphazardly again, we should be selecting people trained to hypothesize not only external threats but internal ones. People who agree how a dispute will be resolved before it occurs. What happens when a Presidential team member disagrees with an Executive Council member? Answer that in advance, or you will answer it in the newspapers." "These are normal stages," I offered, reaching for the comfort of my foreign training. "Any group formation passes through them. Forming, storming, norming. Khatumo has already stormed and normed. Come Khatumo III we will be at the performing stage, where members mature and political compromise becomes the name of the ball-game." "You have a name for every stage except the one you are standing in," said the Lady. Wildlife in Khatumo State ( November 2013) I did not enjoy how accurate that was. Individually, Khatumo folks are successful business leaders, some of them multi-millionaires, some with world-class education and credentials, and yet at the group level we fail at things far smaller than ourselves. Many of us in the diaspora (and here I counted myself, since honesty had already started and it seemed rude to stop it) have earned degrees that have never once been used. What good is an education that cannot put bread on a table, cure a simple disease your own people suffer chronically, or help build a local government led by someone with moral authority? "Speaking of who is the stronger leader among them," she said, "aren't you as strong as your weakest link?" "What do you mean, weakest link?" "See, in Khatumo country, thousands of people cope without clean drinking water and without a clinic. Not enough to eat. Add to that the bickering of the governing old fellows, and life becomes unbearable. A true leader shows courage and humility. You measure his strength not by the number of military tanks staged and showcased, but by the number of health clinics he helped to build, and the number of people whose trust he has earned. "A true leader also asks why the medical practitioner allegedly sent by WHO to serve this Khatumo city has not shown up for the past two years. Why the FM radio unit sent from Mogadishu has never been switched on in Taleh. There is a worthy cause on which to flex a Presidential muscle. Not a title. A title is a socially constructed thing that men internalize as a God-given entitlement, and it has never once dug a well." Beautiful lanscape in Khatumo Country_ near Taleh (Nov. 2013) "Bullying armies from Burco and Bosaso can send bigger bombs," I said, wanting for once to be the one with the hopeful line. "But when the kids in Kalabaydh and Kalshaale colour their school walls with the blessed kalimahs of Khatumo, the enemy's days are numbered. Nothing defeats the will of a modern Dervish. Clear of the clannish thinking that clouds even the learned, this new breed dares to imagine a Taleh that carries its history forward with high-rises and decent health services." Kalabaydh Elementary School (November 2013) "Then let them imagine women in the room," she said. "Is there a single one on the Traditional team?" "Well. Ahh. I don't think so," I hesitated. "See, in Khatumo land we keep things the old way. Respecting the traditional elders." "I will give my respects when Queen Elizabeth of England dictates policy directions to its Parliament and Prime Minister," concluded the Lady. Badbaado Primary- Khatumo State (Nov. 2013) Sitting quietly on the high rows of the stadium, I found myself once again watching a new Khatumo ball-game begin below, and the same three teams jogging out into the same absence of goal posts. "These leaders disappoint me," she said. "The more the men play, the less Khatumo there will be. Unless we can find an alternative." "What alternative?" "An Arrawello, perhaps." And I turned, finally, and looked at her properly, and understood who had been standing behind me for the whole of the second half. "For a thousand years your grandfathers have told one story about me," she said, "and it is always the same story, and it is always about what I am supposed to have taken from men. Not one of them tells the other half. That the wells were dug. That the roads were safe. That the disputes were settled, and quickly, and by somebody. They remember the punishment. They forget the administration." I had no answer to that, and she did not appear to need one. "Then who," I asked, "would you have referee the next Khatumo ball-game?" And I was already wondering whether the correct question was what his name would be, or hers. "It is not even a person. You fool." "Then what is it?" "A constitution. Drafted, written down, and referred to whenever you are in doubt or need help troubleshooting a conflict. Written with the civil society you keep forgetting to invite. And for starters, you may begin with the article that Khatumo is premised on the fact that it is neither Somaliland nor Puntland." The stadium was gone. The sofa was still there, and the television, and Chelsea were a goal up with twenty minutes to play, and my Khatumo Coffee had gone cold in my hand while eleven men in blue moved the ball beautifully towards a goal that was exactly where they had left it. Miracles of Khatumo continues. A. Hindi. t: Somalia Became “Land of Poison”, by Haboon H.Abdi.
x: Somalia has not had a functioning government for many years; the scores of rusty leaking hazardous waste tanks that have been washing up on their shores prove just how many criminals have been exploiting the nation's inability to protect their own waters. Last 23 years illegal toxic waste dumping in Somalia has led to at least thousands deaths and renewed calls from environmentalists for tighter controls over international waste shipments. Unfortunately, Somalia is been used as the world's necropolis for the dumping of toxic materials. Nowadays, it is obvious that this activity is become one of the leading factors that contribute to the hasty deteriorating environment and human health in Somalia. In fact, the effects of illegal dumping can be felt throughout many regions across Somalia. On this remark, most of Somalia's long sea shores and fishing sources have been polluted by chemicals products that are released from toxic waste materials that are illegally dumped into Somalia. Every year tons of poisonous chemical sludge was dumped at various sites around the long seashore of Somalia, leading to thousands of reports of people suffering from vomiting, diarrhea, and nosebleeds. There were no any investigations are underway to find out a floated toxic waste tankers shows every spot at Somali beaches. Meanwhile, the incident has many Somali diaspora and environmental groups decrying a lack of proper controls over the international waste recycling market. As waste management has become globalized, countries with civilian unrest, no environmental law enforcement, or weak legislative frameworks have become prime targets for illegitimate hazardous-waste dealers, the groups contend. "Unscrupulous dealers are also globalized," said Somali diaspora member. "Wastes always follow the path of least resistance," Diaspora member said. "What is happening in Somalia is a series of unfortunate events linked to greed. That toxic waste should have never reached lawless Somalia." Why Somalia? The following is lists of factor that influence illegal dumping in Somalia: (a) The Long Civil War: The Somali people have not yet recovered from many of the suffering that their societies experienced during the longest civil war in Africa. Also, added to this fact is the humiliation that many Semi-tribal states in Somalia attempts to control the vast natural resources in Somalia by many enterprises and foreign governments has contributed to the modern idea of "neocolonialism," which in conjunction with other factors could be held accountable for many of the scandals and corrupted politicians that are currently taking place in Somalia, including illegal dumping. In addition, these two factors disrupted the development of many Somali institutions, destabilized the economy of many tribal-state regions throughout the country leaving Somali people ever dependent from the outside world. Also, this condition of dependency has been exacerbated in recent decades with the demand of raw materials. This, in conjunction with many other factors, has caused of many scandals and corruptions in Somalia, including illegal dumping. (b) Furthermore, the ongoing civil war, lawless and other socio-economic and political upheavals in Somalia have made the country a save heaven for any sort of illegal activity. (c) Also, Somalia's reliance on foreign aid has made it vulnerable for illegal trade. (d) On the other hand, Internal Tribal-Semi States Divisions in Somalia can also be blamed to some extend for the lack of progress on human right issues in Somalia, giving chance to this type of activities as it is with the case of illegal dumping. (e) Moreover, the low cost of illegal dumping in Somalia, $ 1.5 per gallon of toxic waste compared to $350 per gallon in the US and in EU, is another factor that can also be blamed for the disproportionate dumping of toxics in Somalia. Details about why the waste was allowed to enter the lawless Somali seashore remain hazy. Numerous diaspora voices to UNEP at Nairobi, seeking comment went unanswered. What is it Toxic Waste? The widely used term toxic waste is difficult to define. In this fact sheet it includes substances harmful to life and the environment, i.e. wastes with any of the following characteristics: poisonous, radioactive, flammable, explosive, corrosive, carcinogenic (causing cancer), mutagenic (damaging chromosomes), teratogenic (causing defects in the unborn) or bioaccumulative (accumulating in the bodies of plants and animals and thus in food chains). Toxic or poisonous wastes are produced during industrial, chemical, Hospitals, and biological processes. Even household, office and commercial wastes contain small quantities of toxic wastes (e.g. batteries, old pesticides and their containers). Examples of Toxic Wastes PCBs: (poly-chlorinated biphenyls): Non-flammable, insulating material used by big electrical networks such as Eskom. Dioxins: Produced by burning chlorine-containing substances e.g. plastics; the manufacture of iron and steel, and some organic chemicals e.g. herbicides. Found in bleached white paper. In Somalia there were no labs and scientist to determine Dioxins in fish and sea water. Heavy metals: Widespread industrial use, such as in cadmium and nickel plating. Found in batteries (mercury, cadmium, lead) and leaded petrol. Radioactive waste : By-product of nuclear power generation and used in medicine (e.g. cancer therapy). In Conclusion: Somalia lacks the technology, Scientists and adequate laboratories to characterize and analyse toxic wastes, and UNEP wasn't answer numerous diaspora and Somali scientist voices to help their country. (1)Haboon Haji is a graduate student at East Africa University of Buuhoodle-Khatumo State of Somalia

t: The Reason Behind Creating Tribal Federal States in Somalia!!
x: The Reason Behind Creating Tribal Federal States in Somalia!!? For some Neighbor States like Ethiopia and Kenya it is a Strategy for defeating the Pan-Somalia Dream. "The smaller pieces of a pie are easier to eat it". Many historians of Somalia are convinced that Tribal community political ideologies only developed in contact with the European 'thinking about tribes' which the missionaries and colonial officers brought to Somalia. Early 19th Century Colonialism drew borders which did not exist and threw together Somali people who would ordinarily have lived together into one Somali nation and nationality. During the colonial era, the Europeans used various approaches to dominate the Somali tribes. In varying degrees, the French, British and Italians tried to transform the Somalis into five colonial regions in Horn of Africa (NFD, Ogadenia, French Djibouti, British Colonial and Italian Colonial).. Like any cultural group that was arbitrarily divided at the Scramble for Africa, Somalis will not stop with the dream of reunification of all their population into a greater Somalia. To begin with, as the Dervishes Liberation era dawned in the late 1910s and SYLs, SNL and USP early 40s, the West realized the great threat posed to its hegemony by an independent and unified Somalia in Horn of Africa. Nowhere is the neo-colonial thumbprint more evident than in Somalia. Defining back the relation between colonialism and tribal states, you have to know the distinction in between two phases of colonialism; that is, active and passive colonialism. The former refers to the conquest of a people followed by the direct control (or domination) of the same by the conquerors using a combination of measures such as military coercion and dominance of major internal institutions such as the polity. The latter, on the other hand, represents what is commonly referred to as neo-colonialism or the extension of especially economic domination of a people beyond the attainment of self-rule. The second phase of colonization is associated with practices, policies and structures inherited from the first phase. These constitute a colonial legacy that, in our view, impacts on the extent of corruption in independent Somali nation. Recently the passive colonialists had organized group of Somali tribal leaders to select the members of the Somalia's future legislatures (4.5 tribal systems). Remember to collect taxes; the colonial governments mostly relied on local Somali tribal leaders and especially chiefs. Where chiefs did not exist or were uncooperative, new ones were appointed by the colonial powers. Above all, to motivate chiefs to generate as much tax revenue as possible, and do so with zeal, the colonial administrations allowed them to retain a part of it. To understand the association between corruption and the practice of divide and rule one must reflect on some of the methods utilized to sustain it. Those tribal state warlords groups such as Somaliland and Puntland are enjoying a privileged status in the ex-colonial administration were rewarded with easy access to western aid donations and political assistances. The modernization of tribal war and politics have paved the way for an aggressive build-up of illegal high powered firearms in Somalia posing a serious threat to development, progress and freedom. All public properties, including schools, seaports, airports and aid posts, in Somalia are subject to possession by Tribal States such as Puntland and Somaliland. Today Somalia is at the mercy of Western political interference propaganda and media conglomerates which relentlessly paint the country as one beset by poverty, piracy, terrorists crime, diseases and endless wars which has to be rescued by foreign aid workers and sanctimonious celebrities at Nairobi and Addis Ababa…Because of those UN Envoys, Aid donors, and foreign NGO's Somalis have lost their way, culturally, politically and economically. Contemporary forms of Tribalism in Somalia are growing in magnitude and incessantly adopting violent forms. It is a barrier to peace, violates the dignity of human race across social and tribal boundaries, and holds back victims development. The Current Somali man/woman will think of himself as a Hawiye, Darod, Digil-Mirifle or an Isaaq rather than, say, a Somali. This is because the tribal states that exist in Somalia now did not exist before the civil war. Today, the influences of the tribes, tribal beliefs, and tribal chiefs are increasing. Loyalty to the Somali Nation is gradually being replaced by loyalty to a Tribal State, and tribal conflicts become strong and have resulted in civil wars and monumental slaughter of peoples. The expectation that you can develop a Tribal state in Somalia exclusively is just too wishful thinking. The thinking that you can hate a tribe or a group of people and expect to build a prosperous and for the Tribal State itself survive is quite myopic. The problem in governing Somalia squarely lies with tribalism, a shakily United Nations NGOs, greed, external interests, poverty, and skewed allocation of resources dating from many years in the past and so on. Recently the Hope of Somalis has been cheated out of the corrupted legislatures (parliamentarians) members and their owners of so called "UNSOM, USAID, UNDP, Qatar, and AMISOM" using voting manipulations they sought are indisputable. What is reprehensible is the cynical manner in which the Somali people's genuine anger has been orchestrated into 'tribal states conflict.' That is the danger that Somalia faces-unscrupulous leaders backed by foreign interests dividing their people in order to cling to power. These are leaders without vision, traitors to Pan-Somali ideals, squandering the sacrifices of heroes who gave their lives for the dream of a free United Pan-Somalia. My Fellow Somalis, Tribalism is pervasive, and it controls a lot of our actions, readily overriding reason. Think of the inhuman things we do in the name of tribal unity and tribal mini-states. Wars are essentially, and often quite specifically, tribalism. Genocides are tribalism – wipe out the other group to keep our group safe – taken to madness. My fellow Somali citizens before a year is over we require no less than an imaginative, intelligent and broadly accepted constitution and elected anti-corruption and anti-tribalism leaders like Mrs. Yussur Abrar . Otherwise we are not out of the woods yet. By: Haboon Haji Abdi (1) Buhotle -Khatumo State –Somalia, Horufadhi English Section.

t: Khatumo People Sends Message…to PM Abdiweli Sh Ahmed, by. Habon H.Abdi.
x: "We need your Government Help like other regions!" It was a day of celebration as an estimated thousands Khatumo State community members rallied to welcome PM Abdiweli's nomination as prime minister of Somalia. The peaceful march and rally was organized by the SSC civil society and diaspora Groups, with input by other individuals, community groups, organizations and numerous volunteers. Despite the Somaliland Tribal secessionist militiamen harassments in Laascaanood , Xuddun , and Ceerigaabo cities, demonstrators were in high spirits as they gathered outside of the Taleex, Laascaanood, Ceerigaabo and Buuhoodle, which served as a rally point. Many SSC community members carried Khatumo and Somali flags along with home-made signs in an effort to make a clear statement that they are opposed to the balkanization of Somalia and supporting the New Prime minister. A caravan of cars, and horses that were filled with Khatumo and Somalia flags, accompanied the walkers as they literally marched to the beat of their own drum ( Jaandheer ). Additionally, passionate speeches from SSC community educators, elders, students, local political leaders and community members were given, all citing major concerns and opposition against the Somali government's intent to negotiate unilaterally with Northern Secessionist tribal groups (Isaaqs). Among them was a class of grade 5 students from Buuhoodle, who shared a letter they wrote to PM Abdiweli. One student began…" Dear Prime Minister Abdiweli; we the grade five students from Buuhoodle School in Khatumo Sate of Somalia we do need your government education development act too". Several students chimed in to help read the entire message which ended on this note, "we have the right to get teachers, get curriculum, and we want to our own Khatumo State government to stay in control of our security, and education because they are the ones that know what's best for us like all other Somali children". It is clear that Khatumo State people is opposed to the proposed Istanbul meeting between the Northern tribal secessionists and Federal government for many reasons, but mainly because the SSC community has been successfully managing its own economic development and education system since the 1991s. Interim Khatumo State President, Hon. Indhosheel says the new PM has to guarantee the membership of Khatumo State in the future of Somali Federal states as we now know it. "The main dangers of the proposed Istanbul meeting are the possible loss of control over our Unity system". Indhosheel also says the Istanbul act(s) makes no mention regarding the Unionist Sate of Khatumo. Another area of Khatumo concern is that under the new PM administration, the federal government could appoint a Ministerial group to ensure Khatumo State get its allocated development programs from the international aid donors through Somali federal government. "I'm proud to say that Khatumo Sate people were amongst the first to state clearly supported PM Abdiweli," said President Indhosheel, who was among the speakers at the rally held after the march. "We have carried the message across Somalia that we will not accept the balkanization of Somalia, nor will we tolerate the arrogance of the Tribal Northern Secessionists (Somaliland)." "Khatumo, take notice," concluded Indhosheel. "We will not allow any other tribal state (Somaliland and Puntland) to undermine our children's education, we will not allow those tribal States to undermine our rights and we will remain united to defend the integrity of Somali Unity and our community . " (1) Haboon Haji Abdi: Undergraduate Student at East Africa University-Buhootle Khatumo State of Somalia

t: Let’s Converge in Taleh to Perfect Khatumo
x: The development of a political power system reflects upon the values and the ways in which a society thinks of itself and the world. It also relates to the fundamental right to own and propagate an exclusive identity that comes with an unquestionable respect. The world reacts positively to the establishment of a bureaucratic system, having characteristics like hierarchy and chain of command. In other words, international community deals with fully structured governments in Somalia. The upcoming convention in Taleh is geared toward creating a modern framework of government with sustainable procedures for leadership succession. An emerging political system will probably consist of legislative, Judiciary and the executive. There will be much excitement about the creation of a legislative branch, but passing the first law by a Khatumo assembly will cause the highest emotional state. The people are looking forward to a structured system whose authorities intend to deliver services and consolidate administrative control of the state's territorial jurisdiction. Everywhere, loyal Khatumites are prepared to attend the Convention en masse as it will be a historical event that will lay the foundation for a solid administration with full-fledged governmental institutions. It is inconceivable to miss out on the formation of a constitutional order that represents the essence of one's existence. Diasporas are expected to go to Taleh long before local participants reach the venue and witness the inauguration of the 2 nd regime of Khatumo State. The Diasporas from all continents are encouraged to converge in Taleh to show their commitment to the objectives of the convention. They must hold seminars, workshops, and presentations on good governance to minimize the obsession with clan-based power sharing. As most of them will be coming from the developed world, they will have the advantage of transferring their knowledge by teaching the value of consensus driven political culture where voting decides the course of action. Adopting contemporary political system enables the state to organize civil societies, allocate resources, and formulate policies that can improve standards of living. This can be made possible by leaders that fully comprehend today's political difficulties and have the competencies to determine the future direction of Khatumo State. The Diasporas may be able to supply such qualified individuals who could dwell on effective and non-corrupt public administration. All capable compatriots should volunteer to run for positions in the anticipated establishment. This will furnish the system with much-needed human resources. Skilled workforce and technocrats can definitely create functional institutions, and help the State achieve its challenging goals with lightening speed. Khaatumo Forum strongly urges members of the Diaspora to change the course of history by joining the new government. The Khatumo Forum for Peace, Unity and Development info@khaatumoforum.org

t: IN SOMALILAND SPEAK NO EVIL OF THE PRESIDENT
x: A few days ago Universal television released a comedy sketch-characterized by irony and caustic wit- ridiculing President Silanyo of Somaliland. I watched the sketch and found it to be funny and harmless. My head spin in disbelief when Somaliland information minister Abdullahi Mohamed Ukuse interpreted the satirical sketch as a mean spirited condescension that was a threat to Somaliland integrity .I guess the sketch stuck a pin into the self-importance balloon of Somaliland president. According to the minister the television station is guilty of using a comical language and caricature of the President. The Minister took the sketch as a personal attack against the president of Somaliland and decided to suspend Universal television. If the minister actions doesn't make every Somaliland citizens heads spin, then I don't know what it will take to make them smell a rat! The spectacle of Minister Ukuse suspension of Universal television clearly shows that Somaliland government have the carte blanche to do just about anything in the name of protecting the image of the president of Somaliland. This archaic and retrogressive laws used by Somaliland authorities to suppress opposing views- not less a satirical one- is very discouraging! The only aim of taking Universal television out of the air in Somaliland is to intimidate the journalist not to dare antagonize the powerful hierarchy of Somaliland. This case demonstrates that if Somaliland wants to have a livelier and more diverse media landscape, then they need to evolve in guaranteeing press freedom. Without freedom of press the whole of Somaliland ambitions comes apart at the seams. It would be difficult to defend a president who is contemptuous of criticism. Somaliland authority needs to restore their credibility by allowing Universal television back in the air and calm the roiling waters that threaten to drown this young ambitious country! The unique role of the Somali press is to inform the public on wide range of matters, from local Somali events to those of international significance. Freedom of the press is largely instrumental to freedom of expression of the public and both will seem to flow naturally in a democratic state. If Somaliland wants to protect an image it should be their image of how they practice democracy. Presidents all over the world are ridiculed and I don't know why president Silanyo should be of exception. They are lucky that Universal television don't use animal character and descriptions corresponding to Somalia/Somaliland leaders. I guess the respected Minister don't know that this kind of comical sketch is often used to point out pomposity, absurdities and hypocrisy of governments, which I'm guessing he just proved it effortlessly! I must say congrats to the producers of the universal television for the clarity of their message and the wit of their execution. Giving up the right to ridicule leaders should strike any Somali media personalities as the unholiest of deals to accept as a media While we are still talking about Satire and Somali media we might as well mention the great Somali editorial cartoonist Amin arts. At time when most of Somali websites represent the interests of certain clan, Amin Arts succeeded in creating a visually imaginative or bitingly satirical cartoons of Somali politics of the day! Amin daily images speaks to the Somalis in a visceral way. His critical eye and rapier paint brush made him one of the leading cartoonist of Somali speaking people. Occasionally he also does get in trouble with sensitive Somalis who think he is directly attacking their so called leaders. Amin influence could be counted in the number of Somali politicians he made cringe at the sight of their caricature in his web page! We need more of Amin Arts in Somali media circus! Mohamed Ahmed

t: In Remembrance of Engineer Mohamed Burale Farah (Doxore), By Ali H, Abdulla.
x: Mohamed Burale Farah It is with great pain and sorrow that we announce the sudden departure of our colleague and friend Mr. Mohamed Burale Farah who passed away on Sunday 26 January 2014 in Addis Ababa where he served on the Board of Directors for The Horn Economic and Social Policy Institute (HESPI), an independent, non-profit think tank and consultancy firm established in 2006 for the countries of the Horn of Africa in particular and developing countries at large. Mohamed was a Somali intellectual with an MSc in Water Resources (Irrigation and Drainage Engineering). He also completed several post-graduate studies in agriculture, water resources development planning and on-farm water resources management from USA Universities of Washington, Utah and Colorado. After graduation, he worked for various local and international organizations like FAO in many countries around the world. Mohamed will be remembered by many Somalis in Addis Ababa after the collapse of the Somali government where he was known to have helped many to cope with the new reality in Somalia. He was kind, generous and very helpful to all Somalis. Apart from his professional work in many developing countries around the world, he will perhaps be remembered most for his role in the establishment of the Khatumo State of Somalia with five other colleagues such as Dr. Ali Isse Abdi, Dr. Ali Khalif Galaydh and Engineer Jama Abshir Adde. The 6 men were later known as the G6 or group of six which was later expanded to G11 and acted as a consultative Council for the Khatumo State of Somalia. Mohamed was the dynamo behind the group and will definitely leave behind a big gap that will be hard to fill. Many Khatumites will remember him and his 5 other colleagues for the arduous long trek from Addis to Taleh, the historic city where Khatumo was born, a journey that was filled with hardship and risks. As Northern unionists, the secessionist regime of Somaliland tried block their safe return to their homes but fortunately failed to do so. Our thoughts and prayers are with the immediate family Mohamed leaves behind and the larger Khatumo family that will miss him tremendously because of his tireless efforts to promote their just cause. May the Lord Almighty forgive Mohamed for any trespasses and have mercy on his soul. For Khatumo Consultative Council (G11) Ali H Abdulla Email Email: aliegeh@gmail.com

t: Khatumo Torontonians Celebrates 2nd. Anniversary of Khatumo State of Somalia
x: Press Release: Second Anniversary of Khatumo State of Somalia. January 12, 2014 marks the second anniversary of the creation of Khatumo State of Somalia. Is Khatumo State's two years of existence and the freedom of the SSC people truly a cause for celebration? This question shall be debated by the real sons and daughters of Khatumo State of Somalia and not the enemies and the traitors, as we reflect on the two years journey we have travelled together. In January 2012, delegates from across all parts of the SSC regions met at the convention in Taleh and have overwhelmingly supported the establishment of Khatumo State of Somalia. After two years of its establishment and fighting relentless wars from many fronts Khatumo State of Somalia finally enjoys its place in the history of Somalia's modern political and social spectrum. The Khatumo State of Somalia has made significant progress on the political front. For example, Khatumo State signifies the freedom and self-determination as a fundamental right for the SSC people. It is the symbol of dignity and the right of the SSC people to decide for themselves. It is recognized as the symbol of peace, unity and social justice and the world admires at our transition within a short period from a colonized region to an independent rightful state. Apart from the neighboring administrations who are outright enemies of our young state, there are so many forces from within who are persistently attempting to derail its progress and wants to see Khatumo fail. However, the aims of those who want to bring Khatumo to its knees will always be doomed to fail. Once all SSC people get the taste of freedom, Khatumo State shall obtain an unstoppable momentum and shall overcome difficulties and transcend all barriers. Soon, the SSC people will hold its Khatumo III conference in Taleh which the citizens enjoy freedom to choose the manner in which the state is governed through elections and other forms of public participation. The SSC people will not be dictated to do whatever the two neighboring enemies wanted. This Conference shall also lay a firm foundation for our government based on the will of the people, and we continue to improve on it. All of these achievements and milestones are testimony that we have a lot to be grateful for as we approached the third year of the Freedom of the SSC regions. By celebrating our successes, no one is saying there are no remaining challenges ahead. Instead, we acknowledge that we still have a long way to go and the difficulties ahead are of similar magnitude to the successes. But we are committed in our determination to ensure freedom and better life for all SSC people. Khatumo Forum for Peace, Unity and Development info@khaatumoforum.org

t: An Open Letter to Abdiweli Mohamed Ali Gas. President-elect of Puntland
x: Puntland president: A Wali Gaas Saturday, January 18, 2014: To begin with, The Khatumo Forum for Peace, Unity and Development would like to congratulate you on your election win, which returned hope and inspiration for all brotherly peoples of Khatumo and puntland States. The Khatumo Forum for Peace, Unity and Development is writing this letter to you in the capacity of an advocacy organisation which unites not only the voices of Khatumo Diaspora but enjoys the overwhelming support of the entire SSC population as well as the traditional and political leaders of Khatumo State of Somalia. The Forum is deeply concerned about the lack of positive reciprocal reaction from your leadership with regards to the Political Statement and good will gesture issued by Khatumo Leaders as soon as you were elected to the presidency of Puntland in January 8, 2014. The political Leadership of the Khatumo State of Somalia was expecting from Puntland leadership to reciprocate positively and contribute constructively to develop a two-way street_political and social relationship. The SSC people of Khatumo State reiterated in many instances the importance of positive engagement and support between the Khatumo and Puntland States is essential for the success of our transition to equal partners in the national political platform. Without this two way support, collaborative political vision and dedicated leadership, it is doubtful that both the Khatumo and Puntland States will survive under the pressures, manipulations and machinations of the leaders of the federal government and those of Somaliland as well. Throughout our history in North East Somalia, our two peoples have have enjoyed and celebrated a deep socio-traditional and ancestral lineage. We believe that despite the competing political interests, Puntland and Khatumo can afford nothing less than the preservation of this genetic relationship through peaceful negotiations between the two administrations. Additionally, You may be aware that, as equl partners, the SSC people have made every effort in every level of their social and political echelons and presented comprehensive terms of positive engagement to their counterparts in Puntland. But, it was very unfortunate that every political move taken by the old Puntland leadership was detrimental to the good-will gesture of the SSC people and to Khatumo State of Somalia. Mr. Farole's collaborative political treason with the Somaliland administration during their invasion of LasAnod on October 17, 2007 and his adherence to its occupation policies by signing unscrupulous and ruthless sell-off deal of the SSC Capital, with the Somaliland secessionist enemies; His conspiring tactics and actions to undermine Khatumo forces' ability to defend the SSC regions during the Kalshale and Sooljoogto genocide. Although the SSC people have sacrificed hundreds of courageous heroes in those wars, The Khatumo forces unwaveringly defended their land. Thanks to Allah and to the strong and unbreakable determination and will power of Khatumo people; Another fresh example is the recent war of November 28, 2013. This Tragedy in Taleh was ochestrated by Puntland's well mechanized forces massacring innocent civilians, destroying their properties and creating mass desplacement of hundreds of Khatumo citizens. The fall-out of Faroole's destructive projects against Khatumo, and his romance with the secessionist policies of Somaliland have created a deep fracture of anguish and polarized the political stand of the Khatumo people. When the SSC people were treated as second-class citizens and not as equal partners in the Puntland deal, when UN aid shipments destined to their cities were denied access, when 17 illegal MP's were manufactured as having the legitimacy of their Khatumo constituents, and when 69 armed Technicos were dispatched from Garowe, determind to kill their own, The people of Khatumo had enough. Truly, Apart from the above outrageous conspiracies, treason, wars and years of impoverishment of all Sectors of the SSC economy, these policies led to the rightful declaration of Puntland and Khatumo as separate regional administrations under a United Somali Federation. This political economy of underdevelopment applied to the SSC regions has also undermined the trust of the SSC people. In many ways as you have testified in your campaign platform, the two people's partnership has been betrayed by Puntland in so many different ways; Hence the SSC people's self-determination not to abide by Puntland's original tenets, democratically deciding overwhelmingly to create their own Khatumo State of Somalia. As you are aware, in January 12, 2012 delegates from all walks of life of Khatumo people have convened at Taleh and deliberated the pros and cons of creating their own state. In the end, they came up with the internationally celebrated decision to proclaim the Khatumo State of Somalia with three member presidential council to run the state. This is where your part comes in during your tenure as the then Prime Minister of Somali Provisional Government. Your historic letter of recognition of the Khatumo State of Somalia as a member of the Federal States was celebrated and resonated across all SSC regions of Khatumo State. Setting Policy Priorities: Although it will take time and work to make up for what the SSC people have lost, we believe that your new administration shall create a new opening to reverse the trend of the previous Puntland Administration by:- 1. As your administration sets its policy priorities, it is imperative for your government to mend the severely broken relationship with the SSC people by avoiding to recycle the hateful and destructive policies of the previous Puntland leadership towards the Khatumo State of Somalia and the SSC people. 2. recognizing the legitimacy of Khatumo State of Somalia. This is a critical issue to the success in bringing about a rebirth of quality relationship based on trust and mutual respect between the two brotherly states, i.e. Khatumo State and Puntland State. 3. not pursuing the divide to rule and destroy agenda of your predecessor against the Khatumo people as it will scratch the old wounds and open new ones. After all, this would be the anti-thesis of your recent pledge to search for "Unity" in the region. Conclusion Mr. President Your administration will not escape history. It will be remembered through the difficult but realistic and necessary decisions it makes from today on. This is the moment to shake off and throw aside old hateful habits and projects that reinforce the status quo. Now is the moment to reinvest in the very definition of our brotherly relations; charting a new peaceful course towards a more secure, prosperous and sustainable future for both Khatumo and Puntland States. With respectful salutations, warm regards and best wishes The Khatumo Forum for Peace, Unity and Development info@khaatumoforum.org

t: Starting 01.11. 2014 You can send your money from Toronto to: Taleh, Buhodle, Boame and all SSC Khatumo Region
x: A new way to pay your Taxes in SSC Khatumo region. Hi there! Imagine every time you send back home 100 dollars.
